- **Self-check vectors:** both match exactly. A gives `82a5353d` (score 25.38, fall tick 1035, 166 entries); B gives `2e8858d7` (score 10.93, fall tick 457, 48 entries). The page re-runs both at load and sets `BENCH_REPORT.selfCheck` from the result.

## Strategy design

- **Build:** a fixed build/upgrade order with a turret type per slot (mostly cannons, plus flak and bolts), bought as soon as affordable above a gold reserve held for interest while nothing is close to leaking. Once the board is fully upgraded, some slots are sold and rebuilt as lance, frost or flak.
- **Targeting:** each candidate is scored by armour-aware effective damage, summed over the splash for cannon and flak. That is weighted by enemy type (menders first), by time-to-leak urgency, and by an emergency multiplier just before a leak. Frost picks unslowed runners and wisps.
- **Tuning:** order, types and weights were tuned by simulated annealing on random seeds. Custom targeting was worth about 7 waves over default targeting in the first comparison.
- **Known weak spot:** in a few of the 600 games I inspected, an early runner slipped through or a wisp-heavy wave leaked mid-game. One earlier candidate collapsed to 33 on such a seed; the chosen one did not on the 1000 I ran.

## Implemented, with simplifications

All six systems (board, enemies and turrets, combat visuals, fall, HUD, audio) are implemented and reported as "full". The simplifications listed in `BENCH_REPORT`:

- Turret heads snap to the bearing of their last shot instead of tracking continuously.
- An enemy removed during a tick is held at its last position until that tick.
- Desaturation is a framebuffer-copy greyscale pass in the same renderer, with a CSS filter only as fallback.
- The 12-per-second shot-sound cap uses a wall-clock window.

On seed 42 the keep falls at 99.05 s, so the collapse and desaturation get only the last 0.95 s of the replay.

- **Audio:** the audio code ran without errors, but I never listened to it, so mix levels and the character of each sound are untested.

- An enemy removed during a tick is held at its last position until that tick.
- Desaturation is a framebuffer-copy greyscale pass in the same renderer, with a CSS filter only as fallback.
- The 12-per-second shot-sound cap uses a wall-clock window.

On seed 42 the keep falls at 99.05 s, so the collapse and desaturation get only the last 0.95 s of the replay.

## Not verified

- **Audio:** the audio code ran without errors, but I never listened to it, so mix levels and the character of each sound are untested.
- **Frame rate:** not measured on a real GPU. The headless test used software rendering (about 22 fps), which says nothing about the 60 fps target. `measuredFps` starts as `null` and is filled in at runtime from the first 2 s of playback on the viewing machine.
- **Strategy-facing fields:** the vectors do not exercise `target()`. The strategy relies on `EnemyView.x`/`y` being centi-tiles and on `slowed` being truthy when slowed. It deliberately avoids `speed`, turret `x`/`y` and `range`, whose exact form the spec leaves open.
